title: Quick Berbere Beef Roast with Garlic Collard Greens
summary: Designed for busy weeknights, this speed-focused Ethiopian roast delivers robust aromatic depth without long oven times. Tender sirloin roast is cut into uniform medallions, rubbed with a vibrant homemade berbere spice mix, and seared hot in seasoned niter kibbeh. The pan drippings form a rich gravy enhanced with shallots, minced garlic, fresh ginger, and red wine. Accompanied by quick-sauteed collard greens and crisp red onion slices, this dinner balances heat and rich savory warmth. Using elevated heat and smaller meat cuts shortens roasting time drastically while retaining juicy flavor. A splash of lemon juice cuts through the richness of the spiced butter, bringing balance to the plate. Serve this dish alongside teff flatbreads or steamed rice for a complete weeknight meal that tastes like a weekend feast. The spiced beef rub seals in moisture rapidly while the berbere reduction gravy infuses every bite with garlic, cardamom, and chili notes.

steps.step: Preheat your oven to 425 degrees Fahrenheit and set an oven-safe cast iron skillet on the stove.
Trim excess fat from the sirloin roast and slice it into four thick, uniform steak pieces.
Pat the beef surfaces dry using kitchen paper towels to encourage crisp browning during searing.
Combine the berbere spice, ground korarima, fenugreek, sea salt, and black pepper in a small bowl.
Rub the dry spice blend thoroughly onto all sides of the beef medallions to form a coating.
Heat two tablespoons of spiced clarified butter in the cast iron skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Lay the seasoned beef pieces into the hot pan, taking care not to overcrowd the skillet surface.
Sear the meat undisturbed for three minutes until a dark, flavorful crust forms on the bottom side.
Flip the steaks over using sturdy tongs and sear the reverse side for an additional two minutes.
Transfer the cast iron skillet containing the seared beef directly into the preheated hot oven.
Roast for twelve minutes until an instant-read thermometer inserted in the center reads 135 degrees.
Carefully remove the skillet from the oven using thick oven mitts and place it on a trivet.
Transfer the roasted beef to a cutting board, tent with foil, and let rest for eight minutes.
Retain all rich roasting juices and caramelized brown bits remaining in the hot cast iron skillet.
Place the skillet with reserved juices back over medium heat on the stovetop burner.
Add the sliced shallots and diced red onion to the hot pan, stirring into residual meat fat.
Saute the onions for four minutes until translucent and soft around the caramelized edges.
Stir in the minced garlic, ginger paste, ground cumin, ground coriander, and smoked paprika.
Cook the spice mixture for ninety seconds until vibrant aromatics fill your kitchen space.
Spoon the tomato paste into the pan and stir constantly to cook out raw acidity for two minutes.
Pour in the dry red wine while scraping up stuck roasted drippings from the pan bottom with a spoon.
Simmer the wine rapidly for three minutes until the liquid volume reduces by half.
Whisk the cornstarch into cold beef stock until smooth, then pour the liquid into the skillet.
Bring the sauce to a gentle boil, stirring continuously as it thickens into a glossy gravy base.
Stir in the fresh lemon juice and ground cloves to brighten the deep warm spice flavor profile.
Taste the reduction gravy and adjust seasoning with a pinch of sea salt or berbere if needed.
Reduce burner heat to low and keep the rich gravy warm while finishing the greens dish.
Pour any accumulated juices from the resting beef plate right back into the sauce pan.
Wash the collard greens thoroughly under cool running water and pat them completely dry with towels.
Strip the tough woody stems away from collard leaves and slice the leaves into thin ribbons.
Heat vegetable oil and remaining spiced clarified butter in a separate large skillet over medium-high heat.
Slice the jalapeno peppers into thin rings, keeping seeds for extra heat if desired by diners.
Add jalapeno slices and remaining minced garlic to the pan, frying for one minute until fragrant.
Toss the shredded collard greens into the skillet and toss quickly using tongs to coat in oil.
Pour in apple cider vinegar and cook greens for five minutes until tender yet brightly colored.
Season greens with a dash of salt and black pepper before removing skillet from the burner.
Slice the rested berbere beef roast against the grain into thin, juicy dinner slices.
Arrange a warm bed of sauteed garlic collard greens on one side of four serving plates.
Fan out the sliced spice-rubbed beef roast alongside the cooked green vegetables neatly.
Ladle the hot berbere pan reduction gravy generously over top of the roasted beef slices.
Garnish plates with chopped fresh cilantro leaves for a burst of color and herbaceous aroma.
Serve immediately while hot for a fast, flavorful Ethiopian roast meal on weeknights.
